zh: 冲突只发生在连续相同的字符之间。把单词切成若干段“连续相同字符”，不同段之间的分界处本来就不相同，可以各段分别处理。
一段长度为 L 的相同字符，把其中第 2、4、6… 个字符改掉就能消除所有相邻相同，共 floor(L/2) 次；改成的字母只需与左右两边都不同，26 个字母总够用，也不会影响到相邻段。少于这个次数则必然留下两个相邻且未改动的相同字符。
对每个单词用双指针扫描：从 i 出发把 j 移到第一个与 s[i] 不同的位置，这一段长度为 j−i，答案加上 (j−i)/2（向下取整），然后令 i=j。扫描完输出该单词的答案，每个单词一行。
en: Conflicts only occur between consecutive equal characters. Split the word into runs of identical characters; the boundaries between different runs already differ, so each run can be handled on its own.

For a run of L equal characters, changing the 2nd, 4th, 6th, ... characters removes every adjacent equal pair, using floor(L/2) changes; each new letter only has to differ from its two neighbors, which 26 letters always allow, and it does not affect the neighboring runs. Any fewer changes would leave two adjacent unchanged equal characters.

For each word, scan with two pointers: from i, move j to the first position whose character differs from s[i]; the run has length j - i, so add (j - i) / 2 rounded down to the answer, then set i = j. After the scan print that word's answer, one line per word.

explanationEn:
## Approach

Split the word into maximal runs of one letter. Characters on either side of a run boundary already differ, so runs can be handled independently: a run of length `L` needs at least `floor(L/2)` replacements, and that many always suffice. The answer is the sum of `floor(L/2)` over all runs.

For example, in `boook` the run `ooo` needs only its middle `o` changed: `floor(3/2) = 1`.

## Proof of correctness

- Lower bound: inside a run of length `L`, the adjacent pairs `(1,2), (3,4), ...` are `floor(L/2)` pairs that share no character. Each pair is equal and needs at least one of its characters changed, and one replacement changes one character, so it fixes at most one of these pairs. The run therefore needs at least `floor(L/2)` replacements. Pairs from different runs do not overlap either, so the bounds add up.
- Achievability: in each run, change the 2nd, 4th, 6th, ... characters (`floor(L/2)` of them). The neighbours of a changed character are unchanged and show at most two distinct letters, while the alphabet has 26, so we can always pick a letter different from both. Afterwards adjacent characters inside the run differ, and the run's end characters are either untouched or chosen to differ from the outside neighbour, so boundaries stay distinct.

The bounds match, so the answer is correct.

## Complexity

O(|s|) time and O(1) extra space per word.

## Pitfalls

- Do not count equal adjacent pairs: `ooo` has 2 of them but needs only 1 change.
- For an even-length run the last character is changed, and it must also differ from the character after the run; with 26 letters there is always a choice.
